evidence: Temporary probe ZzProbeTest in integration-tests (deleted afterwards), run with `mvn -o -B test -pl integration-tests -am -Dtest=ZzProbeTest` under JDK 8 at head ae7f8fa: voidVisit_defaultOrder (test-env order [BaseVoidHandler, VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandler, VisitVoidHandler]) passes, while voidVisit_queueHandlerFirst (the same cached HandlerUtil list with the queue handler moved first) fails: entry 3 is not voided. Core 2.7.4: HandlerUtil.getHandlersForType sorts only by @Handler.order (both are Integer.MAX_VALUE by default) over ServiceContext.getRegisteredComponents, which copies into a `new HashMap<>(...)`, so ties fall into HashMap order and that order depends on which VoidHandler beans exist in the deployment. main's own test VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandlerTest.java:122 admits that it 'depends on it running after core's BaseVoidHandler'. Fix verified: I temporarily restored a voidVisit branch in the advice that copies visit.getVoidReason/getVoidedBy/getDateVoided. With it, voidVisit_queueHandlerFirst passes, and VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandlerTest (7), PatientWithQueueEntriesVoidHandlerTest (13), VisitWithQueueEntriesDeleteAdviceTest (2) and VisitWithQueueEntriesValidatorTest (8) all still pass. Not run: an actual RefApp deployment at this head.

evidence: git diff 36b2040 ae7f8fa -- VisitWithQueueEntriesDeleteAdvice.java shows the voidVisit branch deleted and a 'purgeVisit' name guard added inside the merge commit, while the PR description still says the advice intercepts voidVisit. I drove the real path with a throwaway integration test (since deleted) that registered N extra no-op VoidHandler singleton beans, cleared HandlerUtil's cache, called visitService.voidVisit(visit of queue entry 3, "deleted") and flushed. With extra=0 the order was BaseVoidHandler, VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandler, VisitVoidHandler: visitVoided=true, entryVoided=true. With extra=18 it was VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandler, VisitVoidHandler, BaseVoidHandler: visitVoided=true, entryVoided=FALSE. In that same extra=18 state, registering the 36b2040 advice via Context.addAdvice gave entryVoided=true. A HashMap simulation calibrated against the real extra=0 order flips at 18 extra beans (25 in total, past the 24-entry resize threshold). Main's VisitWithQueueEntriesSaveHandlerTest#shouldVoidQueueEntriesWhenVisitIsVoidedThroughVoidVisit (line 120) pins the outcome only for the test context's 7 VoidHandler beans. Fix: restore the voidVisit branch in the advice (reading args[1] as the reason, with includedVoided and the proxy privileges), or remove the handler's order-dependent void branch so there is a single deterministic owner.
